Assuming atomic folder rename/local POSIX behavior can break cloud object workflows.

Choose format from schema, row/column access, interoperability, evolution and workload needs—not

FAILURE TO CATCH
Calling Parquet universally best ignores streaming/interchange/debug and nested-schema needs.
C3-04-L03 — Columnar storage, statistics and compression
MENTAL MODEL
Column chunks, row groups, statistics and compression let engines avoid reading irrelevant bytes.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Writing Parquet alone does not guarantee pruning if row groups/statistics/filters are poorly aligned.
C3-04-L04 — Partitioning strategy and pruning
MENTAL MODEL
Partition on selective, stable access dimensions at sensible cardinality; prove filters prune
files/partitions.
FAILURE TO CATCH
High-cardinality partitioning creates tiny files and metadata overhead.
C3-04-L05 — Small-files problem and compaction
MENTAL MODEL
Compaction changes physical layout, not logical rows; trigger it from measurable file-size/count
evidence.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Compacting without parity checks can drop/duplicate data, while vacuum is a separate destructive
lifecycle action.
C3-04-L06 — Catalogs, metadata and table namespaces
MENTAL MODEL
Catalogs give durable logical table identity and metadata boundaries independent of physical file paths.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Hard-coded paths make table identity brittle and bypass governance/metadata.
C3-04-L07 — Lake vs warehouse vs lakehouse + open table-format trade-offs
MENTAL MODEL
Compare architecture/table formats by transaction, evolution, engine, governance and maintenance
requirements.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Declaring Delta/Iceberg/Hudi a universal winner hides workload and ecosystem trade-offs.
C3-04-L08 — Delta transaction log and ACID guarantees
MENTAL MODEL
A versioned transaction log defines committed table state and supports atomic changes/time travel.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Reading raw files directly can observe uncommitted/obsolete physical files and bypass table
semantics.
C3-04-L09 — Schema enforcement and schema evolution
MENTAL MODEL
Reject incompatible writes by default; evolve schema deliberately and distinguish additive from
breaking changes.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Auto-merging every schema change can silently widen/break downstream contracts.

Page 2
Diagnostic review
FORMAT/LAYOUT
Choose Parquet/table layout deliberately; preserve row/key/metric semantics across conversion.
SCHEMA EVOLUTION
Add calibration_batch deliberately as nullable/controlled additive field; prove base rows remain
readable and downstream contract is understood.
MERGE/UPSERT
Match on stable reading_id; one source row per key; corrected key updates and new key inserts.
LATEST-STATE VALIDATION
Result must have one row per key, expected latest metric sum and no duplicate corrected key.
TIME TRAVEL
Capture pre-merge version, post-merge version and historical read evidence. Historical result is
table-state evidence, not date filtering.
PARTITION/PRUNING
If partitioned, choose useful low/moderate-cardinality field and show filter/pruning evidence rather than
assuming it.
COMPACTION
If small-file maintenance is used, prove row/key/metric parity before vs after compaction.
RETENTION/VACUUM
Treat vacuum as separate destructive lifecycle action; state how it changes time-travel/rollback
guarantees.
LAYER CONTRACT
State bronze/raw fidelity, silver canonical schema/key and gold/serving grain/ownership. New field
must not silently propagate as breaking change.
Green-but-wrong states to reject
•
Table write succeeds but old and corrected versions both remain.
•
Schema auto-merge succeeds but downstream type/contract is now ambiguous.
•
Compaction reduces file count but logical metric/key parity was never checked.
•
Historical query is simulated by filtering current rows instead of reading the actual prior table version.

Dedupe/validate correction source, MERGE on reading_id. Changed proof: another key receives
update+insert and final row count/metric reconcile.
IF SCHEMA EVOLUTION FAILED
Classify calibration_batch as additive optional field, update contract explicitly and prove old rows
remain valid. Changed proof: add a second optional field with controlled null/default behavior.
IF TIME TRAVEL FAILED
Capture explicit version/history and read the prior version before retention removal. Changed proof:
compare two table versions around a new correction.
IF COMPACTION FAILED
Capture file/row/key/metric controls before, compact, then prove logical parity. Changed proof:
compact a different partition/file set.
IF VACUUM/RETENTION FAILED
Separate optimize from vacuum; choose retention from recovery/audit requirement. Changed proof:
explain which historical version would become unreadable after a proposed retention cut.
IF LAYER CONTRACT FAILED
Write explicit bronze/silver/gold schema/grain/owner/quality rules. Changed proof: classify one additive
and one breaking schema change and show different handling.

Source/base+correction controls and stable-key statement.
•
Pre/post merge row/key/metric reconciliation.
•
Schema evolution evidence for new column.
•
Table history + explicit prior-version read.
•
Partition/pruning or file-scan evidence where relevant.
•
Compaction parity evidence; vacuum/retention decision kept separate.
•
Layer/table contract and operator handoff.

review never unlocks them.
